newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE LOOKING FOR ANOTHER DERBY WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE LOOKING FOR ANOTHER DERBY WIN.

text.p: Fenerbahce, buoyed by a crucial victory against Istanbul rivals Galatasaray, have turned their attention to another important derby match as they bid to pull away at the top of the Turkish league.
Following their 3-2 win over their arch-rivals on Sunday, Fenerbahce will face Istanbul's other major team Besiktas next weekend.

To the untrained eye, the rivalry is every bit as fierce as the one that exists between Galatasaray and Fenerbahce, but locals say it is slightly less intense -- often leading to slightly more relaxed game.

"We have only won one match. There is no point in exaggerating things. We are now thinking about Besiktas. We still have 13 weeks to go. We want to be champions for the second time in a row," said Fenerbahce manager Ridvan Dilmen.

Fenerbahce were beaten by Besiktas in a Turkish cup match last Wenesday and are keen to gain immediate revenge and league points and fly to the Mediterranean resort town of Antalya on Tuesday to prepare for their second successive local derby.
"We still have some problems and we aim to solve these at Antalya ahead of the Besiktas match."
After beating Galatasaray on Sunday, Fenerbahce pulled level with them at the top of the table -- although Galatasaray stay top on goals.

But new Fenerbahce coach Todor Veselinovic, who took over from sacked Brazilian Sebastiao Lazaroni last Thursday -- believes that Fenerbahce can only improve and was delighted with Sunday's win which came with a goal from Nigerian striker Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha and two from Bosnian forward Elvir Bolic.
"The Fenerbahce you have just seen was not the real Fenerbahce. In the future we will play much much better, and let no one doubt that we will become champions," said the Yugoslav coach.
The Turkish media feted the derby match as a welcome return to excitement in the league.
"The league has just begun. The two rivals are head-to-head," said the daily Hurriyet.
"The Devil has struck down the leaders," said the daily Yeni Yuzyil, referring to manager Dilmen's nickname as a player.
Galatasaray, meanwhile, consoled themselves that they remained top.

"If we had won this match, we would have run away with the championship. But we are still leaders on goal average and plan to stay top. There are still a lot of matches to be played and we will be champions," coach Fatih Terim said.
"You get very few opportunities to score in such a derby match. What is important is to make the most of them. But we were unable to do that," he said.

Galatasaray were particularly let down by their international striker Hakan Sukur, who squandered five clear chances in the first half and was virtually anonymous throughout the second half and their cause wasn't helped by the second half dismissal of their Romanian playmaker Gheorghe Hagi.
Galatasaray have a relatively easy match against mid-table Sariyer next week, but they will be missing the vital contribution of Hagi, who went after two bookings.
